nodes.name: CoCe-DHBDC Powder Synthesis
nodes.procedure: Co(OAc)₂·4H₂O (0.65 mmol) and Ce(NO₃)₃·6H₂O (0.13 mmol) were dissolved in DMF (15 ml) under ultrasonication (30 min) to yield solution A, and DHBDC (0.78 mmol) was dissolved in DMF (20 ml) to obtain solution B. Subsequently, solutions A and B were mixed, followed by the sequential addition of anhydrous ethanol (2 ml), deionized water (2 ml) and triethylamine (0.5 ml), with ultrasonication (5 min, 40 kHz) to form a brown precipitate. The resulting CoCe–DHBDC catalyst was collected by centrifugation, washed with ethanol and deionized water, subjected to overnight solvent exchange in ethanol/water (1/1, v/v) and freeze-dried. For large-scale synthesis, all reagents were proportionally scaled up.

nodes.name: CoCe-MOF Electrodeposition
nodes.procedure: A electrodeposition solution was prepared by dissolving DHBDC (0.05 M), Co(NO₃)₂·6H₂O (0.083 M), Ce(NO₃)₃·6H₂O (0.017 M) and triethylamine hydrochloride (0.03 M) in 10 l of DMF/H₂O (80/20, v/v) under 30 min ultrasonication at room temperature. The pretreated NF, mounted in an epoxy-coated conductive Cu frame, served as the cathode, and two parallel Ir-coated Ti meshes (230 mm × 230 mm, 25 mm spacing) were employed as anodes. Electrodeposition was performed with electrolyte recirculation (1 l min⁻¹) using a two-step current program: 10 mA cm⁻² for 2 min followed by 40 mA cm⁻² for 6 min. The resulting MOF electrode was sequentially washed with ethanol and deionized water, followed by vacuum drying at 60 °C for 2 h.

nodes.characterization_summary: CoCe–DHBDC and Co–DHBDC possess identical diffraction peaks isostructural to Co-based MOFs; characteristic peaks at 6.68° and 11.64° for (110) and (300) planes shift to smaller angles in CoCe–DHBDC indicating lattice expansion.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The crystalline nature of the MOFs... was confirmed by powder X-ray diffraction and the corresponding Pawley refinement (Supplementary Figs. 6,7). ... characteristic peaks of CoCe–DHBDC at 6.68° and 11.64° associated with (110) and (300) crystallographic planes shift to a smaller angle position compared with Co–DHBDC

nodes.characterization_summary: Scattering vector values of Co–DHBDC at 0.481 and 0.834 Å⁻¹ shift to 0.475 and 0.826 Å⁻¹ after Ce doping, attributed to lattice distortion from (110) and (300) planes.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Grazing incidence wide-angle X-ray scattering (GIWAXS) was employed to investigate this lattice distortion (Fig. 2b and Supplementary Fig. 9). Diffraction intensity profiles... reveal that scattering vector values of Co–DHBDC located at 0.481 and 0.834 Å⁻¹ shift to 0.475 and 0.826 Å⁻¹ after Ce doping

nodes.characterization_summary: Co K-edge XANES derivative peak shifts from 7720.4 eV (Co–DHBDC, Co²⁺·²⁸) to 7721.2 eV (CoCe–DHBDC, Co²⁺·⁴¹); Ce L₃-edge shifts from 5722.4 to 5721.6 eV indicating charge redistribution.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The derivative peak of Co K-edge XANES (7,720.4 eV) for CoCe–DHBDC shifted to a higher energy position (7,721.2 eV)... By contrast, the derivative peak of Ce L3-edge XANES shifts from 5,722.4 to 5,721.6 eV

nodes.characterization_summary: FT-k³-weighted EXAFS shows Co–O bond at ~1.60 Å compresses from 1.61 Å (Co–DHBDC) to 1.56 Å (CoCe–DHBDC); Co–Co distances at 2-3 Å.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fourier-transformed k³-weighted EXAFS (FT-EXAFS) analysis and fitting (Fig. 2f and Supplementary Fig. 17). The peaks observed in the R-space at ~1.60 Å are attributed to the Co–O bond... Ce doping induces a compression of the Co–O bond length from 1.61 to 1.56 Å

nodes.characterization_summary: High-resolution XPS spectra of Co 2p and Ce 3d support orbital interaction and charge redistribution.
nodes.evidence_snippet: This orbital interaction is further supported by high-resolution X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy spectra of Co 2p and Ce 3d (Supplementary Fig. 14)

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ XAS shows Co oxidation state increases and coordination number decreases with potential; Co–Co distance elongates at 1.0 V then contracts at 1.3-1.5 V indicating reconstruction to cobalt hydroxide-like then oxyhydroxide-like phases.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In situ XAS was conducted to monitor the potential-dependent evolution of the Co oxidation state... EXAFS... revealed that a slight elongation of the Co–Co distance (2–3 Å) at 1.0 V... marked contraction of both Co–O bond lengths and Co–Co distances were observed

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ Raman shows CoCe–DHBDC undergoes earlier and more complete transformation to Co(OH)₂- and CoOOH-like phases than Co–DHBDC.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In situ Raman spectroscopy (Fig. 6d) demonstrates that CoCe–DHBDC undergoes an earlier and more complete transformation into Co(OH)₂- and CoOOH-like phases than Co–DHBDC
